title: Am I Sikh enough?
hookLine: cut hair, no amrit, no Punjabi: the Sikh code defines a Sikh by belief, and the gurdwara door is open at every stage

lines: A CAR IN THE PARKING LOT.
SHORT HAIR. NO GURMUKHI. YEARS AWAY.
cards: A car in a gurdwara parking lot. The engine's off, and nobody gets out. Inside, a young man with short hair is running through a list.
My grandfather wore a turban; I don't. I can't read Gurmukhi. I haven't been here since I was a kid.
Will people look at me? Am I even allowed to call myself Sikh? A lot of people sit in that car.
Some sit there for years. Today, the question, and an honest answer.

teach.b: Start with the word. Sikh means learner, and a learner, by definition, isn't finished. Then the code.

The Sikh Rehat Maryada, the code of conduct most gurdwaras follow, defines a Sikh first by belief: in one God, the ten Gurus, the Guru Granth Sahib and the Gurus' teaching, and the tenth Guru's amrit, with allegiance to no other religion.
It doesn't open with a haircut or a language test. Uncut hair does matter deeply in Sikhi. It's a vow for those who take amrit, and many Sikhs hold that every Sikh should aim to keep it.
Sikhs differ, sometimes strongly, on how that applies to someone who isn't there yet. That's a real conversation, and your Keeper is a good person to have it with.

teach.h: THE DOOR IS OPEN TO ALL.
teach.b: What isn't in doubt is the door. Langar feeds whoever sits down. Cover your head, take off your shoes, and you're in.
Many Sikhs answer this exact worry with an old saying: the house of Nanak is open to all. And not reading Gurmukhi?

Plenty of Sikhs, especially those who grew up far from Punjab, are in exactly that spot, and many learn as adults. So the useful question isn't, am I Sikh enough? It's the learner's question: what's my next step?
For one person it's walking in. For another, one bani, or one letter.
That's Sikhi: the Sikh way, a path you walk, not a badge you earn before you start.

how: The Sikh Rehat Maryada defines a Sikh by belief; gurdwaras welcome anyone who covers their head and removes their shoes, and Sikhs live their Sikhi at many stages, from first visit to amrit.

games.q: a friend with short hair says they feel like a fake Sikh and has stopped going to the gurdwara. what's the answer from today?
o: wait until your hair has grown back.
the door is open: start where you are, as a learner.
games.why: Sikh means learner, and the Gurus kept an open door. the next step can be as small as walking in.

practice: Picture that parking lot again, and this time it's you in the car, exactly as you are today: your hair, your Punjabi or the lack of it, your questions.
Open the door, walk to the shoe rack, slip your shoes off, cover your head, and step inside. Notice any voice that says you're too late, or not enough; let it speak, then let it go quiet.
Sit down on the floor beside everyone else, and rest with the breath.
